text.p: A Libyan government official met with the Mauritania ambassador on Tuesday, another sign that relations between the two countries were warming after Tripoli withdrew its ambassador in 1995 when Mauritania established ties with Israel.

The official Libyan news agency JANA reported that (Pan-Arab) Unity Affairs Minister Jomaa al-Fezzani met in Tripoli with the Mauritanian ambassador to discuss "the relations between the two countries and means to develop them."
Earlier this month a reconciliation meeting was held in Tunis between Libyan and Mauritanian officials sponsored by Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali.

Libya in November 1995 recalled its ambassador from Nouakchott and said it would cut off economic aid to the North African state in retaliation for Mauritania's decision to establish ties with Israel.
Nouakchott accused Tripoli of trying to destabilise it and in January this year arrested three Mauritanian politicians it accused of having "dubious ties" with Libya.
